import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Kronecker coefficient

The Kronecker coefficients $g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ are the multiplicities in the decomposition of a
tensor product of two irreducible representations of the symmetric group $S_n$ into irreducible
representations: $V_\mu \otimes V_\nu = \bigoplus_\lambda g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} V_\lambda$.
They can be computed from the irreducible characters $\chi^\lambda$ of $S_n$ by
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n}
  \chi^\lambda(\sigma) \chi^\mu(\sigma) \chi^\nu(\sigma).$$

The Wikipedia list of unsolved problems asks to "give a combinatorial interpretation of the
Kronecker coefficients" (a question of Murnaghan, 1938). The standard formal version of this
problem, conjectured in Mulmuley's GCT6 and recorded by Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter, is that the
Kronecker coefficients have a `#P`-formula: there are a polynomial $p$ and a polynomial-time
computable $0$-$1$ function $F$ with
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \sum_{\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{p(\langle\lambda\rangle, \langle\mu\rangle,
  \langle\nu\rangle)}} F(\lambda, \mu, \nu, \sigma),$$
where $\langle\lambda\rangle$ is the total bit-length of the parts of $\lambda$ written in binary.
In other words, the map $(\lambda, \mu, \nu) \mapsto g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$, with the partitions
given in binary, is in the counting class `#P`. The weaker form in which the partitions are given
in unary is stated as a variant.

Mathlib has no Specht modules and no parametrisation of the irreducible characters of $S_n$ by
partitions, so this file defines $\chi^\lambda$ through the Frobenius character formula: for
$\sigma \in S_n$ of cycle type $\rho$ (fixed points counted as $1$-cycles), $\chi^\lambda(\sigma)$
is the coefficient of $x_1^{\lambda_1 + n - 1} x_2^{\lambda_2 + n - 2} \cdots x_n^{\lambda_n}$ in
$$\prod_{1 \le i < j \le n} (x_i - x_j) \cdot \prod_k p_{\rho_k}(x_1, \dots, x_n),$$
where $p_k = x_1^k + \dots + x_n^k$ is the $k$-th power sum and $\lambda_i = 0$ for $i$ larger
than the number of parts of $\lambda$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kronecker coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kronecker_coefficient)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- C. Ikenmeyer, K. D. Mulmuley, M. Walter, *On vanishing of Kronecker coefficients*,
  Comput. Complexity 26 (2017), [arXiv:1507.02955](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.02955),
  Section 1.3.
- K. D. Mulmuley, *Geometric Complexity Theory VI: the flip via positivity*,
  [arXiv:0704.0229](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.0229).
- R. P. Stanley, *Positivity problems and conjectures in algebraic combinatorics*, Problem 10.
- W. Fulton, J. Harris, *Representation Theory: A First Course*, Formula 4.10
  (Frobenius formula).
-/

noncomputable def vandermonde (n : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ :=
  ∏ i : Fin n, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (X i - X j)
blocks.docstring: The Vandermonde product `∏_{i < j} (X i - X j)` in the variables `X 0, …, X (n - 1)`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Matrix.det_vandermonde` (a matrix determinant over a commutative ring, not the multivariate polynomial); no MvPolynomial Vandermonde in Mathlib.
justification.name: KroneckerCoefficient.vandermonde
justification.why_needed: The alternant ∏_{i<j}(X i − X j) in `MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ` for the Frobenius formula.

noncomputable def powerSumProd (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ :=
  (σ.partition.parts.map (psum (Fin n) ℤ)).prod
blocks.docstring:
The product `p_{ρ_1} ⋯ p_{ρ_k}` of the power sums `p_k = ∑ i, (X i) ^ k` over the cycle type
`ρ` of the permutation `σ ∈ S_n` (the fixed points of `σ` are counted as `1`-cycles).

justification.closest_existing_considered: `MvPolynomial.psum` (single power sum; used as building block) and `Equiv.Perm.partition`.
justification.name: KroneckerCoefficient.powerSumProd
justification.why_needed: Product of power sums over the cycle type of a permutation (p_ρ), the symmetric-function image of a conjugacy class.

blocks.name: powerSumProd
blocks.text:
/-- The product `p_{ρ_1} ⋯ p_{ρ_k}` of the power sums `p_k = ∑ i, (X i) ^ k` over the cycle type
`ρ` of the permutation `σ ∈ S_n` (the fixed points of `σ` are counted as `1`-cycles). -/
noncomputable def powerSumProd (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ :=
  (σ.partition.parts.map (psum (Fin n) ℤ)).prod

noncomputable def character (μ : n.Partition) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ℤ :=
  coeff (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i : Fin n => part μ i + (n - 1 - i))
    (vandermonde n * powerSumProd σ)
blocks.docstring:
The value `χ^μ(σ)` of the irreducible character of `S_n` indexed by the partition `μ` of `n`
at the permutation `σ`, defined by the Frobenius character formula: the coefficient of
`X 0 ^ (μ_1 + n - 1) * X 1 ^ (μ_2 + n - 2) * ⋯ * X (n - 1) ^ μ_n` in the product of the
Vandermonde product and the power sums of the cycle type of `σ`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FDRep.character` (abstract characters of a given representation, but no representation indexed by partitions); no Schur polynomials in Mathlib.
justification.name: KroneckerCoefficient.character
justification.why_needed: The irreducible character χ^λ of S_n indexed by a partition; Mathlib has no Specht modules and no parametrisation of S_n irreps by partitions.

blocks.name: character
blocks.text:
/-- The value `χ^μ(σ)` of the irreducible character of `S_n` indexed by the partition `μ` of `n`
at the permutation `σ`, defined by the Frobenius character formula: the coefficient of
`X 0 ^ (μ_1 + n - 1) * X 1 ^ (μ_2 + n - 2) * ⋯ * X (n - 1) ^ μ_n` in the product of the
Vandermonde product and the power sums of the cycle type of `σ`. -/
noncomputable def character (μ : n.Partition) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ℤ :=
  coeff (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i : Fin n => part μ i + (n - 1 - i))
    (vandermonde n * powerSumProd σ)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def kroneckerCoefficient (κ μ ν : n.Partition) : ℚ :=
  (∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), (character κ σ * character μ σ * character ν σ : ℤ)) / n.factorial
blocks.docstring:
The Kronecker coefficient
`g^κ_{μν} = (1 / n!) * ∑_{σ ∈ S_n} χ^κ(σ) * χ^μ(σ) * χ^ν(σ)`
of three partitions `κ`, `μ`, `ν` of `n`. It is the multiplicity of the Specht module `V_κ` in
`V_μ ⊗ V_ν`, and hence a natural number.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (searched for Kronecker, Schur, Specht, tableau).
justification.name: KroneckerCoefficient.kroneckerCoefficient
justification.why_needed: The Kronecker coefficient g^λ_{μν} = (1/n!)Σ χ^λχ^μχ^ν, the object of the conjecture.

blocks.name: kroneckerCoefficient
blocks.text:
/-- The Kronecker coefficient
`g^κ_{μν} = (1 / n!) * ∑_{σ ∈ S_n} χ^κ(σ) * χ^μ(σ) * χ^ν(σ)`
of three partitions `κ`, `μ`, `ν` of `n`. It is the multiplicity of the Specht module `V_κ` in

noncomputable def kroneckerCoefficient (κ μ ν : n.Partition) : ℚ :=
  (∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), (character κ σ * character μ σ * character ν σ : ℤ)) / n.factorial

def bitLength (μ : n.Partition) : ℕ :=
  (μ.parts.map Nat.size).sum
blocks.docstring: The bit-length `⟨μ⟩` of a partition `μ`: the total number of binary digits of its parts.

justification.name: KroneckerCoefficient.bitLength

def encodeNat (m : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  (Nat.bits m).flatMap (fun b => [true, b]) ++ [false]
blocks.docstring:
A self-delimiting binary encoding of a natural number `m`: each binary digit `b` of `m`
(least significant digit first) is written as the pair `[true, b]`, followed by a terminating
`false`. Its length is `2 * ⟨m⟩ + 1`, where `⟨m⟩` is the number of binary digits of `m`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Computability.encodeNat` / `finEncodingNatBool` (not self-delimiting, so cannot be concatenated), `Encodable (List ℕ)` via `Nat.pair` (exponential blow-up in the number of parts).
justification.name: KroneckerCoefficient.encodeNat
justification.why_needed: Self-delimiting binary encoding of a natural number, needed to build a binary encoding of partition triples for the poly-time function's input.

def encodePartition (μ : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  (μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).flatMap (fun m => true :: encodeNat m) ++ [false]
blocks.docstring:
A self-delimiting binary encoding of a partition `μ`: for each part `m` of `μ` (in decreasing
order) the list `true :: encodeNat m`, followed by a terminating `false`. Its length is between
`⟨μ⟩` and `4 * ⟨μ⟩ + 1`, where `⟨μ⟩ = bitLength μ`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Fintype`-based `Encodable` instances (encoding length not polynomially related to binary bit-length).
justification.name: KroneckerCoefficient.encodePartition
justification.why_needed: Binary encoding of a partition (parts in decreasing order), polynomially equivalent to the paper's bit-length ⟨λ⟩.

blocks.name: encodePartition
blocks.text:
/-- A self-delimiting binary encoding of a partition `μ`: for each part `m` of `μ` (in decreasing
order) the list `true :: encodeNat m`, followed by a terminating `false`. Its length is between
`⟨μ⟩` and `4 * ⟨μ⟩ + 1`, where `⟨μ⟩ = bitLength μ`. -/
def encodePartition (μ : n.Partition) : List Bool :=

blocks.code:
def encodeTriple (κ μ ν : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  encodePartition κ ++ encodePartition μ ++ encodePartition ν
blocks.docstring:
The binary encoding of a triple `(κ, μ, ν)` of partitions of `n`: the concatenation of the
(self-delimiting) encodings of the three partitions.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `finEncodingListBoolProdListBool` (used for the pair with σ), no existing encoding of partition triples.
justification.name: KroneckerCoefficient.encodeTriple
justification.why_needed: Binary encoding of the triple (λ,μ,ν) as a `List Bool`, the first input of the poly-time function F.

blocks.name: encodeTriple

/-- The binary encoding of a triple `(κ, μ, ν)` of partitions of `n`: the concatenation of the
(self-delimiting) encodings of the three partitions. -/
def encodeTriple (κ μ ν : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  encodePartition κ ++ encodePartition μ ++ encodePartition ν

blocks.code:
def unaryEncodePartition (μ : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  (μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).flatMap (fun m => List.replicate m true ++ [false]) ++ [false]
blocks.docstring:
A self-delimiting unary encoding of a partition `μ`: each part `m` of `μ` (in decreasing
order) is written as `m` copies of `true` followed by `false`, and the whole partition is
terminated by another `false`. Its length is `n + ℓ + 1`, where `ℓ` is the number of parts.

justification.name: KroneckerCoefficient.unaryEncodePartition / unaryEncodeTriple
justification.why_needed: Unary encoding (length linear in n) for the weaker unary variant discussed in the paper.

@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient :
    ∃ (p : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℕ) (F : List Bool × List Bool → Bool),
      Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBoolProdListBool
        Computability.finEncodingBoolBool F) ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (κ μ ν : n.Partition),
        kroneckerCoefficient κ μ ν =
          ((∑ σ : Fin (eval ![bitLength κ, bitLength μ, bitLength ν] p) → Bool,
            (F (encodeTriple κ μ ν, List.ofFn σ)).toNat : ℕ) : ℚ) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients**

Wikipedia: "Give a combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients" (Murnaghan, 1938).

Formal version (Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter, Section 1.3; conjectured in GCT6): the Kronecker
coefficients have a `#P`-formula, i.e. there exist a polynomial $p$ and a polynomial-time
computable $0$-$1$ function $F$ such that for all $n$ and all partitions $\lambda, \mu, \nu$ of $n$
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \sum_{\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{p(\langle\lambda\rangle, \langle\mu\rangle,
  \langle\nu\rangle)}} F(\lambda, \mu, \nu, \sigma),$$
where $\langle\lambda\rangle$ is the total bit-length of the parts of $\lambda$ written in binary.
This is the binary (strong) form of the problem. In Lean the partition $\lambda$ is called `κ`,
and polynomial-time computability of `F` is in the sense of Mathlib's
`Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime`, with input the pair `(encodeTriple κ μ ν, σ)`, where
`encodeTriple κ μ ν` is a binary encoding of `(κ, μ, ν)` of length linear in
$\langle\lambda\rangle + \langle\mu\rangle + \langle\nu\rangle$.

Formal version (Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter, Section 1.3; conjectured in GCT6): the Kronecker
coefficients have a `#P`-formula, i.e. there exist a polynomial $p$ and a polynomial-time

where $\langle\lambda\rangle$ is the total bit-length of the parts of $\lambda$ written in binary.
This is the binary (strong) form of the problem. In Lean the partition $\lambda$ is called `κ`,
and polynomial-time computability of `F` is in the sense of Mathlib's
`Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime`, with input the pair `(encodeTriple κ μ ν, σ)`, where
`encodeTriple κ μ ν` is a binary encoding of `(κ, μ, ν)` of length linear in

@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]

    ∃ (p : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℕ) (F : List Bool × List Bool → Bool),
      Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBoolProdListBool

  sorry

`#P`-formula when the partitions are given in unary, i.e. there exist a polynomial $p$ and a

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Kronecker coefficient

The Kronecker coefficients $g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$ are the multiplicities in the decomposition of a
tensor product of two irreducible representations of the symmetric group $S_n$ into irreducible
representations: $V_\mu \otimes V_\nu = \bigoplus_\lambda g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} V_\lambda$.
They can be computed from the irreducible characters $\chi^\lambda$ of $S_n$ by
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n}
  \chi^\lambda(\sigma) \chi^\mu(\sigma) \chi^\nu(\sigma).$$

The Wikipedia list of unsolved problems asks to "give a combinatorial interpretation of the
Kronecker coefficients" (a question of Murnaghan, 1938). The standard formal version of this
problem, conjectured in Mulmuley's GCT6 and recorded by Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter, is that the
Kronecker coefficients have a `#P`-formula: there are a polynomial $p$ and a polynomial-time
computable $0$-$1$ function $F$ with
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \sum_{\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{p(\langle\lambda\rangle, \langle\mu\rangle,
  \langle\nu\rangle)}} F(\lambda, \mu, \nu, \sigma),$$
where $\langle\lambda\rangle$ is the total bit-length of the parts of $\lambda$ written in binary.
In other words, the map $(\lambda, \mu, \nu) \mapsto g^\lambda_{\mu\nu}$, with the partitions
given in binary, is in the counting class `#P`. The weaker form in which the partitions are given
in unary is stated as a variant.

Mathlib has no Specht modules and no parametrisation of the irreducible characters of $S_n$ by
partitions, so this file defines $\chi^\lambda$ through the Frobenius character formula: for
$\sigma \in S_n$ of cycle type $\rho$ (fixed points counted as $1$-cycles), $\chi^\lambda(\sigma)$
is the coefficient of $x_1^{\lambda_1 + n - 1} x_2^{\lambda_2 + n - 2} \cdots x_n^{\lambda_n}$ in
$$\prod_{1 \le i < j \le n} (x_i - x_j) \cdot \prod_k p_{\rho_k}(x_1, \dots, x_n),$$
where $p_k = x_1^k + \dots + x_n^k$ is the $k$-th power sum and $\lambda_i = 0$ for $i$ larger
than the number of parts of $\lambda$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kronecker coefficient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kronecker_coefficient)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- C. Ikenmeyer, K. D. Mulmuley, M. Walter, *On vanishing of Kronecker coefficients*,
  Comput. Complexity 26 (2017), [arXiv:1507.02955](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.02955),
  Section 1.3.
- K. D. Mulmuley, *Geometric Complexity Theory VI: the flip via positivity*,
  [arXiv:0704.0229](https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.0229).
- R. P. Stanley, *Positivity problems and conjectures in algebraic combinatorics*, Problem 10.
- W. Fulton, J. Harris, *Representation Theory: A First Course*, Formula 4.10
  (Frobenius formula).
-/

namespace KroneckerCoefficient

open MvPolynomial

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The part `μ_{i+1}` of the partition `μ` at position `i` (positions are counted from `0`,
parts are listed in decreasing order), with value `0` beyond the last part. -/
def part (μ : n.Partition) (i : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).getD i 0

/-- The Vandermonde product `∏_{i < j} (X i - X j)` in the variables `X 0, …, X (n - 1)`. -/
noncomputable def vandermonde (n : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ :=
  ∏ i : Fin n, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (X i - X j)

/-- The product `p_{ρ_1} ⋯ p_{ρ_k}` of the power sums `p_k = ∑ i, (X i) ^ k` over the cycle type
`ρ` of the permutation `σ ∈ S_n` (the fixed points of `σ` are counted as `1`-cycles). -/
noncomputable def powerSumProd (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℤ :=
  (σ.partition.parts.map (psum (Fin n) ℤ)).prod

/-- The value `χ^μ(σ)` of the irreducible character of `S_n` indexed by the partition `μ` of `n`
at the permutation `σ`, defined by the Frobenius character formula: the coefficient of
`X 0 ^ (μ_1 + n - 1) * X 1 ^ (μ_2 + n - 2) * ⋯ * X (n - 1) ^ μ_n` in the product of the
Vandermonde product and the power sums of the cycle type of `σ`. -/
noncomputable def character (μ : n.Partition) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ℤ :=
  coeff (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i : Fin n => part μ i + (n - 1 - i))
    (vandermonde n * powerSumProd σ)

/-- The Kronecker coefficient
`g^κ_{μν} = (1 / n!) * ∑_{σ ∈ S_n} χ^κ(σ) * χ^μ(σ) * χ^ν(σ)`
of three partitions `κ`, `μ`, `ν` of `n`. It is the multiplicity of the Specht module `V_κ` in
`V_μ ⊗ V_ν`, and hence a natural number. -/
noncomputable def kroneckerCoefficient (κ μ ν : n.Partition) : ℚ :=
  (∑ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), (character κ σ * character μ σ * character ν σ : ℤ)) / n.factorial

/-- The bit-length `⟨μ⟩` of a partition `μ`: the total number of binary digits of its parts. -/
def bitLength (μ : n.Partition) : ℕ :=
  (μ.parts.map Nat.size).sum

/-- A self-delimiting binary encoding of a natural number `m`: each binary digit `b` of `m`
(least significant digit first) is written as the pair `[true, b]`, followed by a terminating
`false`. Its length is `2 * ⟨m⟩ + 1`, where `⟨m⟩` is the number of binary digits of `m`. -/
def encodeNat (m : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  (Nat.bits m).flatMap (fun b => [true, b]) ++ [false]

/-- A self-delimiting binary encoding of a partition `μ`: for each part `m` of `μ` (in decreasing
order) the list `true :: encodeNat m`, followed by a terminating `false`. Its length is between
`⟨μ⟩` and `4 * ⟨μ⟩ + 1`, where `⟨μ⟩ = bitLength μ`. -/
def encodePartition (μ : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  (μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).flatMap (fun m => true :: encodeNat m) ++ [false]

/-- The binary encoding of a triple `(κ, μ, ν)` of partitions of `n`: the concatenation of the
(self-delimiting) encodings of the three partitions. -/
def encodeTriple (κ μ ν : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  encodePartition κ ++ encodePartition μ ++ encodePartition ν

/-- A self-delimiting unary encoding of a partition `μ`: each part `m` of `μ` (in decreasing
order) is written as `m` copies of `true` followed by `false`, and the whole partition is
terminated by another `false`. Its length is `n + ℓ + 1`, where `ℓ` is the number of parts. -/
def unaryEncodePartition (μ : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  (μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)).flatMap (fun m => List.replicate m true ++ [false]) ++ [false]

/-- The unary encoding of a triple `(κ, μ, ν)` of partitions of `n`: the concatenation of the
unary encodings of the three partitions. -/
def unaryEncodeTriple (κ μ ν : n.Partition) : List Bool :=
  unaryEncodePartition κ ++ unaryEncodePartition μ ++ unaryEncodePartition ν

/-- **Combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients**

Wikipedia: "Give a combinatorial interpretation of the Kronecker coefficients" (Murnaghan, 1938).

Formal version (Ikenmeyer–Mulmuley–Walter, Section 1.3; conjectured in GCT6): the Kronecker
coefficients have a `#P`-formula, i.e. there exist a polynomial $p$ and a polynomial-time
computable $0$-$1$ function $F$ such that for all $n$ and all partitions $\lambda, \mu, \nu$ of $n$
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \sum_{\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{p(\langle\lambda\rangle, \langle\mu\rangle,
  \langle\nu\rangle)}} F(\lambda, \mu, \nu, \sigma),$$
where $\langle\lambda\rangle$ is the total bit-length of the parts of $\lambda$ written in binary.
This is the binary (strong) form of the problem. In Lean the partition $\lambda$ is called `κ`,
and polynomial-time computability of `F` is in the sense of Mathlib's
`Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime`, with input the pair `(encodeTriple κ μ ν, σ)`, where
`encodeTriple κ μ ν` is a binary encoding of `(κ, μ, ν)` of length linear in
$\langle\lambda\rangle + \langle\mu\rangle + \langle\nu\rangle$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient :
    ∃ (p : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℕ) (F : List Bool × List Bool → Bool),
      Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBoolProdListBool
        Computability.finEncodingBoolBool F) ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (κ μ ν : n.Partition),
        kroneckerCoefficient κ μ ν =
          ((∑ σ : Fin (eval ![bitLength κ, bitLength μ, bitLength ν] p) → Bool,
            (F (encodeTriple κ μ ν, List.ofFn σ)).toNat : ℕ) : ℚ) := by
  sorry

/-- The weaker, unary form of `kronecker_coefficient`: the Kronecker coefficients have a
`#P`-formula when the partitions are given in unary, i.e. there exist a polynomial $p$ and a
polynomial-time computable $0$-$1$ function $F$ such that for all $n$ and all partitions
$\lambda, \mu, \nu$ of $n$
$$g^\lambda_{\mu\nu} = \sum_{\sigma \in \{0,1\}^{p(n)}} F(\lambda, \mu, \nu, \sigma).$$
This is the form that corresponds most directly to counting combinatorial objects of size
polynomial in $n$. It is implied by `kronecker_coefficient`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 20 68]
theorem kronecker_coefficient.variants.unary :
    ∃ (p : Polynomial ℕ) (F : List Bool × List Bool → Bool),
      Nonempty (Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime finEncodingListBoolProdListBool
        Computability.finEncodingBoolBool F) ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (κ μ ν : n.Partition),
        kroneckerCoefficient κ μ ν =
          ((∑ σ : Fin (p.eval n) → Bool,
            (F (unaryEncodeTriple κ μ ν, List.ofFn σ)).toNat : ℕ) : ℚ) := by
  sorry

/-- The partition `(1)` of `1` gives the trivial character of `S_1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem character_indiscrete_one : character (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 1) 1 = 1 := by
  have h : (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun _ : Fin 1 => 1) = Finsupp.single 0 1 := by
    ext; simp
  simp [character, vandermonde, powerSumProd, part, Nat.Partition.indiscrete,
    Equiv.Perm.partition, h]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem vandermonde_two : vandermonde 2 = X 0 - X 1 := by
  have : (Finset.Ioi (1 : Fin 2)) = ∅ := by decide
  simp [vandermonde, Fin.prod_univ_two, this]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem powerSumProd_swap : powerSumProd (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 2) 1) = X 0 ^ 2 + X 1 ^ 2 := by
  have h : (Equiv.swap (0 : Fin 2) 1).cycleType = {2} := by
    rw [(Equiv.Perm.isCycle_swap (by decide)).cycleType, Equiv.Perm.card_support_swap (by decide)]
  simp [powerSumProd, Equiv.Perm.partition, h, psum, Fin.sum_univ_two]

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem powerSumProd_one_two : powerSumProd (1 : Equiv.Perm (Fin 2)) = (X 0 + X 1) ^ 2 := by
  simp [powerSumProd, Equiv.Perm.partition, Equiv.Perm.cycleType_one, psum, Fin.sum_univ_two, sq]

/-- The partition `(2)` of `2` gives the trivial character of `S_2`: its value at the identity. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem character_indiscrete_two_one :
    character (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 2) 1 = 1 := by
  have h : (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i : Fin 2 =>
      part (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 2) i + (2 - 1 - i)) =
        Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm ![3, 0] := by
    congr 1
    ext i
    fin_cases i <;> simp [part, Nat.Partition.indiscrete, Multiset.sort_singleton,
      Multiset.filter_singleton]
  have e : ((X 0 - X 1) * (X 0 + X 1) ^ 2 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℤ)
      = X 0 ^ 3 + X 0 ^ 2 * X 1 - X 0 * X 1 ^ 2 - X 1 ^ 3 := by ring
  rw [character, h, vandermonde_two, powerSumProd_one_two, e]
  simp only [coeff_sub, coeff_add, X, monomial_pow, monomial_mul, coeff_monomial, one_mul, one_pow]
  simp [Finsupp.ext_iff, Fin.forall_fin_two]

/-- The partition `(2)` of `2` gives the trivial character of `S_2`: its value at the
transposition. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem character_indiscrete_two_swap :
    character (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 2) (Equiv.swap 0 1) = 1 := by
  have h : (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i : Fin 2 =>
      part (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 2) i + (2 - 1 - i)) =
        Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm ![3, 0] := by
    congr 1
    ext i
    fin_cases i <;> simp [part, Nat.Partition.indiscrete, Multiset.sort_singleton,
      Multiset.filter_singleton]
  have e : ((X 0 - X 1) * (X 0 ^ 2 + X 1 ^ 2) : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℤ)
      = X 0 ^ 3 - X 0 ^ 2 * X 1 + X 0 * X 1 ^ 2 - X 1 ^ 3 := by ring
  rw [character, h, vandermonde_two, powerSumProd_swap, e]
  simp only [coeff_sub, coeff_add, X, monomial_pow, monomial_mul, coeff_monomial, one_mul, one_pow]
  simp [Finsupp.ext_iff, Fin.forall_fin_two]

/-- The partition `(1, 1)` of `2` gives the sign character of `S_2`: its value at the identity. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem character_ofSums_one_one_one :
    character (Nat.Partition.ofSums 2 {1, 1} rfl) 1 = 1 := by
  have h : (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i : Fin 2 =>
      part (Nat.Partition.ofSums 2 {1, 1} rfl) i + (2 - 1 - i)) =
        Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm ![2, 1] := by
    congr 1
    ext i
    fin_cases i <;> simp [part, Multiset.sort_cons, Multiset.sort_singleton,
      Multiset.filter_singleton]
  have e : ((X 0 - X 1) * (X 0 + X 1) ^ 2 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℤ)
      = X 0 ^ 3 + X 0 ^ 2 * X 1 - X 0 * X 1 ^ 2 - X 1 ^ 3 := by ring
  rw [character, h, vandermonde_two, powerSumProd_one_two, e]
  simp only [coeff_sub, coeff_add, X, monomial_pow, monomial_mul, coeff_monomial, one_mul, one_pow]
  simp [Finsupp.ext_iff, Fin.forall_fin_two]

/-- The partition `(1, 1)` of `2` gives the sign character of `S_2`: its value at the
transposition. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem character_ofSums_one_one_swap :
    character (Nat.Partition.ofSums 2 {1, 1} rfl) (Equiv.swap 0 1) = -1 := by
  have h : (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun i : Fin 2 =>
      part (Nat.Partition.ofSums 2 {1, 1} rfl) i + (2 - 1 - i)) =
        Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm ![2, 1] := by
    congr 1
    ext i
    fin_cases i <;> simp [part, Multiset.sort_cons, Multiset.sort_singleton,
      Multiset.filter_singleton]
  have e : ((X 0 - X 1) * (X 0 ^ 2 + X 1 ^ 2) : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) ℤ)
      = X 0 ^ 3 - X 0 ^ 2 * X 1 + X 0 * X 1 ^ 2 - X 1 ^ 3 := by ring
  rw [character, h, vandermonde_two, powerSumProd_swap, e]
  simp only [coeff_sub, coeff_add, X, monomial_pow, monomial_mul, coeff_monomial, one_mul, one_pow]
  simp [Finsupp.ext_iff, Fin.forall_fin_two]

/-- The Kronecker coefficient of the empty partitions of `0` is `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem kroneckerCoefficient_zero :
    kroneckerCoefficient (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 0) (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 0)
      (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 0) = 1 := by
  have h : (Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm fun _ : Fin 0 => 0) = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  simp [kroneckerCoefficient, character, vandermonde, powerSumProd, part, h]

/-- For `S_2`, `V_{(1,1)} ⊗ V_{(1,1)} = V_{(2)}`: the tensor square of the sign representation is
the trivial representation, so `g^{(2)}_{(1,1),(1,1)} = 1` and `g^{(1,1)}_{(1,1),(1,1)} = 0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem kroneckerCoefficient_two :
    kroneckerCoefficient (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 2) (Nat.Partition.ofSums 2 {1, 1} rfl)
      (Nat.Partition.ofSums 2 {1, 1} rfl) = 1 ∧
    kroneckerCoefficient (Nat.Partition.ofSums 2 {1, 1} rfl) (Nat.Partition.ofSums 2 {1, 1} rfl)
      (Nat.Partition.ofSums 2 {1, 1} rfl) = 0 := by
  have hu : (Finset.univ : Finset (Equiv.Perm (Fin 2))) = {1, Equiv.swap 0 1} := by decide
  simp only [kroneckerCoefficient, hu,
    Finset.sum_pair (show (1 : Equiv.Perm (Fin 2)) ≠ Equiv.swap 0 1 by decide),
    character_indiscrete_two_one, character_indiscrete_two_swap, character_ofSums_one_one_one,
    character_ofSums_one_one_swap]
  norm_num [Nat.factorial]

/-- The binary digits of `5` are `101`, so `encodeNat 5 = [1,1, 1,0, 1,1, 0]`. -/
@[category test, AMS 68]
theorem encodeNat_five : encodeNat 5 = [true, true, true, false, true, true, false] := by
  have : Nat.bits 5 = [true, false, true] := by
    rw [show (5 : ℕ) = Nat.bit true 2 from rfl, Nat.bits_append_bit _ _ (by simp),
      show (2 : ℕ) = Nat.bit false 1 from rfl, Nat.bits_append_bit _ _ (by simp), Nat.one_bits]
  simp [encodeNat, this]

/-- The bit-length of the partition `(3)` of `3` is `2`. -/
@[category test, AMS 68]
theorem bitLength_indiscrete_three : bitLength (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 3) = 2 := by
  simp [bitLength, Nat.Partition.indiscrete, Nat.Partition.ofSums, Multiset.filter_singleton]
  decide +kernel

/-- The unary encoding of the partition `(3)` of `3`. -/
@[category test, AMS 68]
theorem unaryEncodePartition_indiscrete_three :
    unaryEncodePartition (Nat.Partition.indiscrete 3) = [true, true, true, false, false] := by
  simp [unaryEncodePartition, Nat.Partition.indiscrete, Nat.Partition.ofSums,
    Multiset.filter_singleton, Multiset.sort_singleton, List.replicate]

end KroneckerCoefficient

items: The informal request 'give a combinatorial interpretation' is formalized as the standard complexity-theoretic version from the cited paper (IMW §1.3) and GCT6: the map (λ,μ,ν) ↦ g^λ_{μν} has a #P-formula. This is stated as a plain conjecture (no `answer(sorry)`), since it is not a yes/no question.

Irreducible characters χ^λ of S_n are defined via the Frobenius character formula: χ^λ(σ) = coefficient of x^{λ+δ} (δ=(n-1,…,0), λ padded with zeros to n parts) in ∏_{i<j}(x_i−x_j)·∏_k p_{ρ_k}, with ρ the cycle type of σ including fixed points (`Equiv.Perm.partition`). Using n variables is valid since every partition of n has at most n parts. Sign/normalisation checked by proven tests (trivial and sign characters of S_2) and scratch checks for χ^{(2,1)} of S_3 (values 2, 0, −1).

The Kronecker coefficient is defined as a rational number (1/n!)Σ_σ χ^κχ^μχ^ν exactly as in the Wikipedia article; it is a natural number mathematically, and the #P-formula equation compares it with a natural-number count cast to ℚ. No reliance on exact integer division.

Input encoding is binary (the strong form, as in the cited paper's definition of a #P-formula): an explicit self-delimiting encoding `encodeTriple` (each part in binary with digits prefixed by `true` and a `false` terminator; each partition terminated by `false`). The polynomial p is evaluated at the encoding length N rather than at the paper's (⟨λ⟩,⟨μ⟩,⟨ν⟩); N is between ⟨λ⟩+⟨μ⟩+⟨ν⟩ and 4(⟨λ⟩+⟨μ⟩+⟨ν⟩)+3, so the two formulations define the same class (standard padding argument).
p is a univariate `Polynomial ℕ` (as in the repo's NP definition in Millenium/PvsNP.lean) and σ ranges over bit strings of exactly length p(N), matching the paper's Σ_{σ∈{0,1}^{p(...)}}.

Polynomial-time computability of F is Mathlib's `Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime` with the repo's `finEncodingListBoolProdListBool` for the input pair (encoded triple, σ) and `Computability.finEncodingBoolBool` for the output, exactly as in Millenium/PvsNP.lean.

Domain restriction |λ|=|μ|=|ν| is built into the types (all three are `n.Partition` for the same n, universally quantified), so no 'g=0 otherwise' convention is needed; #P-membership is unaffected since size-equality is polynomial-time checkable.
Since `λ` is a Lean keyword, the partition λ is named `κ` in the Lean code; the docstrings note this.

reviewer_notes: The Wikipedia entry is a request ('give a combinatorial interpretation'), not a proposition. Following the decomposition notes and IMW §1.3 / GCT6, it is formalized as: ∃ polynomial p (in the three binary bit-lengths) and a poly-time (Mathlib `TM2ComputableInPolyTime`) 0-1 function F on (encoded triple, witness) with g^λ_{μν} = Σ_{σ∈{0,1}^{p(⟨λ⟩,⟨μ⟩,⟨ν⟩)}} F(λ,μ,ν,σ) for all n and all partitions λ,μ,ν of n. Quantifier order (p, F before n, λ, μ, ν) and the ∃…∧ structure were checked. Modeling choices a reviewer should be aware of: (1) Mathlib has no Specht modules, so χ^λ is defined by Frobenius' formula (coefficient of x^{λ+δ} in Δ·p_ρ, n variables, cycle type including fixed points via `Equiv.Perm.partition`); the S_2 tests are proven and I hand-checked χ^{(2,1)}(id)=2 in S_3. (2) g is defined in ℚ by the character-sum formula and compared with the cast witness count; no reliance on exact integer division. (3) The triple is passed to F via an explicit self-delimiting binary encoding whose length is linear in ⟨λ⟩+⟨μ⟩+⟨ν⟩; any polynomially inter-convertible encoding gives an equivalent statement. (4) Witness strings have exactly length p(...), the standard #P definition (the paper's 'polynomially-bounded function' is read as a polynomial). (5) The unary variant (witness length p(n), unary encoding) is included as a separately named weaker variant; it is implied by the binary statement by padding, and is arguably the most direct reading of 'combinatorial interpretation' (objects of size poly(n)). Known theorems mentioned in the article (#P-hardness, GapP membership, NP-hardness of positivity) are not stated, per the notes. No candidate omitted the slot; all reports were 'formalized'. c02's Young-symmetrizer construction is also a faithful definition of χ^λ but was not used because it needs the PvsNP import and has sorry'd tests; c01/c07's Murnaghan–Nakayama definitions looked correct but are harder to audit and have no tests.
